paragraphs.text: Khufu's pyramid
Khufu's tomb rises first, built from limestone quarried on this plateau.
The haul
In this reconstruction, damp sand eases the passage of loaded sledges.
Raising the stone
Here, ramps and levers raise each stone into place.
Khafre's pyramid
Khafre, Khufu's son, builds the second great pyramid on higher ground.
White limestone
White casing stone came by water from the quarries at Tura.
Menkaure's pyramid
Menkaure's pyramid follows: three royal tombs, three separate reigns.

paragraphs.text: Before the stones
An earthwork enclosure stood here centuries before the great stone circle.
Shaping the sarsens
Hammerstones shaped the sarsens; their joints echo skilled woodworking.
Raising the uprights
Here, ropes tip uprights into pits; rubble then secures their bases.
Across the uprights
The film uses timber platforms to raise the stone lintels.
Stones from Wales
Many smaller bluestones came from the Preseli Hills in Wales.
The solstice axis
These stones frame midsummer sunrise and, in the opposite direction, midwinter sunset.

paragraphs.text: Nero's former lake
Vespasian builds an amphitheatre on the site of Nero's lake.
Travertine from Tivoli
The load-bearing piers are built from travertine quarried near Tivoli.
Lifting the blocks
In this reconstruction, treadwheel cranes raise the heavy stone blocks.
Under the vaults
Here, timber supports hold the vaults while the concrete sets.
